title: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head U (Prime Minister's Office)

sections.label: Smart Nation progress and e-residency
sections.summary: An MP moves to cut Head U by $100 and asks about Smart Nation progress and whether e-residency will be rolled out.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Chairman, I beg to move, "That the total sum to be allocated for Head U of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Sir, since the launch of the Smart Nation initiative by the Prime Minister eight years ago, in the formation of the Smart Nation and Digital Government Group five years ago, we were fortunate to have benefited from the coordinated build-up of digital infrastructure, capabilities, talent pool as smart tools through the Smart Nation initiative.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: This preparedness allowed our Government agencies to respond swiftly and act decisively during the COVID-19 crisis.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: But beyond responses to COVID-19, what is the current progress of our Smart Nation efforts and how have we fared so far?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: With our limited space and resources and as the world competes for top talents, will the Government roll out e-residency to allow highly talented digital nomads and businesses to transact and value-add to our economy without having to reside here and compete for our physical space?

sections.label: Seniors and AI, Internet use
sections.summary: A 2020 study found 78% of elderly respondents uncomfortable with AI interpreting medical data, and a 2019 IMDA survey found 58% of seniors above 60 are Internet users.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2020 study supported by the National Medical Research Council showed that 78% of elderly respondents were uncomfortable with AI interpreting their medical data and providing automated advice.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: A 2019 IMDA survey showed that only 58% of seniors above 60 are Internet users as compared to 89% of the general population.

sections.label: Overlapping apps and My Legacy portal
sections.summary: Apps and websites sometimes offer overlapping services, and My Legacy portal users still use CPF, lawyers, SAL and OPG; the MP asks how many signed up.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Since the launch of Smart Nation, many apps and websites have been introduced by various agencies as well as businesses that have tapped on productivity grants.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: As shared by Mr Yip Hon Weng in his Budget speech, these apps and websites sometimes offer overlapping services, bringing about inconvenience to users who have to install and navigate through many apps on their phones.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Another example is My Legacy portal, intended to be a one-stop platform to make estate planning easy and convenient.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: However, Singaporeans today still have to make their CPF nominations through the CPF website, do their Will and Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA) through a lawyer and registering them thereafter through SAL’s Wills Registry and Office of Public Guardian (OPG) respectively.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: How many users have since signed up through My Legacy vault to plan, store and share legal, healthcare and estate matters?

sections.label: Seniors and disabled digital access
sections.summary: Seniors and persons with disabilities often struggle to access digital services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Seniors and persons with disabilities often struggle to access digital services.

sections.label: Singpass app usage and transactions
sections.summary: 3.5 million people use the Singpass app for over 1,700 services, and in 2021 more than 350 million personal and corporate transactions were facilitated via Singpass.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Today, 3.5 million people use the Singpass app to gain access to over 1,700 digital and physical services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In 2021, more than 350 million personal and corporate transactions were facilitated via Singpass.

sections.label: PayNow and CDC vouchers
sections.summary: More than $200 million in PayNow transactions were made daily last year, and CDC vouchers benefited over a million households and over 10,000 heartland merchants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: In fact, more than $200 million in PayNow transactions were made every day last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Another familiar scheme is the CDC vouchers, which have benefited more than a million households and over 10,000 heartland merchants.

sections.label: Beep vending machine distribution
sections.summary: Beep rolled out 1,600 vending machines islandwide, supporting distribution of 30 million masks, 1.3 million TraceTogether tokens and 2.5 million ART kits.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Working with MTI, MOH, PA and GovTech, Beep has rolled out 1,600 vending machines islandwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: They have supported our nationwide distribution of 30 million masks, 1.3 million TraceTogether tokens and 2.5 million ART kits.

sections.label: DigitalforLife and Smart Nation Ambassadors
sections.summary: IMDA launched the DigitalforLife movement, complemented by 4,000 Smart Nation Ambassadors who help residents use digital Government services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA) launched the DigitalforLife movement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: This is complemented by a community of 4,000 Smart Nation Ambassadors, who help our residents feel more comfortable using digital Government services.

sections.label: Singpass app official languages
sections.summary: Since last week, the Singpass app has been made available in Singapore's four official languages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: Since last week, we have started to make Singpass app available in our four official languages.

sections.label: Unanswered incoming calls drop
sections.summary: The percentage of incoming calls that went unanswered dropped from 30% in mid-October to almost zero by end-November.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: The percentage of incoming calls that went unanswered dropped from 30% in mid-October to almost zero by the end of November.

sections.label: Citizen satisfaction with digital services
sections.summary: Continuous efforts raised citizen satisfaction with digital Government services from 73% in 2016 to 85% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mrs Josephine Teo)
sentences.text: For digital Government services, continuous efforts have raised citizen satisfaction from 73% in 2016 to 85% in 2021.

sections.label: Digital Sing dollar readiness
sections.summary: Public documents from the Economic Policy Group conclude Singapore is ready for a digital Sing dollar, though there is no pressing need for its issuance now.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Based on public documents issued by the Economic Policy Group, the conclusion is – to somewhat over-simplify – that Singapore is ready for a digital Sing dollar.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: However, there is no, and I quote, "pressing need for its issuance at this time." MAS has documented a host of advantages associated with, ultimately, adopting a digital Sing dollar.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: First, doing so could help crowd out alternative, volatile digital private currencies, especially low-value meme cryptocurrencies that have been an outlet for speculated access.

sections.label: Digital Sing dollar counterfeiting benefits
sections.summary: A trackable digital Sing dollar would help reduce counterfeiting and illicit use, given the $1,000 bill MAS still mints.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
sentences.text: Third, a digital Sing dollar, especially one that is trackable by MAS, will help reduce the incidence of counterfeiting and being used for illicit activities, especially given that the largest denomination bill that MAS still mints is still relatively large at $1,000.

sections.label: Limited purpose bank accounts
sections.summary: Investigations can last months to years, and MAS has worked with retail banks to open limited purpose accounts for higher-risk individuals.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These investigations can take any time between several months and years, which are a long time to function without access to basic banking facilities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I understand MAS has been working with the larger retail banks to open limited purpose bank accounts for individuals that banks assess to pose a higher risk of being implicated in financial crimes.

sections.label: Retail CBDC case not compelling
sections.summary: MAS has assessed that the case for a retail CBDC in Singapore is not compelling.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At this point, MAS has assessed that the case for a retail CBDC in Singapore is not compelling.

sections.label: Fast domestic payments availability
sections.summary: FAST, PayNow and SGQR mean cheap and fast domestic payments are widely available via bank-based payment systems.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The roll-out of FAST, PayNow and SGQR in recent years means that cheap and fast payments are widely available domestically via bank-based payment systems.

sections.label: Project Orchid technical competencies
sections.summary: MAS has embarked on Project Orchid to build technical competencies needed to issue a digital Singapore dollar if decided.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: MAS has embarked on Project Orchid to build the technical competencies necessary to issue a digital Singapore dollar, should we decide to do so in future.

sections.label: MAS prepares but no immediate case
sections.summary: MAS will continue to prepare for possibly issuing a digital Singapore dollar but sees no immediate case for doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Overall, MAS will continue to prepare for the possibility of issuing a digital Singapore dollar, but does not see an immediate case for doing so.

sections.label: Bank pilot exercise feedback
sections.summary: The pilot exercise lets banks obtain feedback and refine the product before accounts launch officially in the second half of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The pilot exercise will allow banks a chance to obtain feedback and refine the product before the accounts are officially launched in the second half of this year.

sections.label: Fertility rate and marriages survey
sections.summary: TFR was 1.10 and marriages 19,430 in 2020, and a TODAY survey found many young Singaporeans hesitant about marriage and children.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, our Total Fertility Rate (TFR) at 1.10 and number of marriages at 19,430 in 2020 were at their lowest points for the decade.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: While the number of marriages showed signs of returning to pre-pandemic levels, having children remains a hesitation in many young Singaporeans' minds.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In a Youth Survey conducted by TODAY newspaper with 1,066 respondents between the ages of 18 and 34 published in November 2021, only about half of the unmarried respondents felt that marriage was important and less than half said it was important or very important to have a child in the future.

sections.label: Working from home in 2021
sections.summary: In 2021, 46% of employed residents in Singapore worked from home due to the COVID-19 situation.

sentences.speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: In 2021, 46% of employed residents in Singapore were working from home due to the COVID-19 situation.

sections.label: Childcare sick leave agreement
sections.summary: The Government does not disagree with the speaker on childcare sick leave.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
sentences.text: The Government does not disagree with me when it comes to childcare sick leave.

sections.label: Resident births and TFR 2021
sections.summary: Preliminary resident births in 2021 were around 34,200, and TFR was 1.12, a slight recovery from 1.10 in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: The preliminary number of resident births in 2021 remained similar to 2020, at around 34,200.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our TFR was 1.12 last year, a slight recovery from the historic low of 1.10 in 2020.

sections.label: Marriage and parenthood survey findings
sections.summary: The 2021 M&P survey found eight in 10 young singles aspire to marry and have children, and over nine in 10 married Singaporeans want at least two children.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: From our 2021 M&P survey, eight in 10 young singles aspire to get married and have children, and over nine in 10 married Singaporeans want at least two children.

sections.label: Baby grant to parents
sections.summary: Parents of over 44,000 babies have received the grant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Parents of over 44,000 babies have received the grant.

sections.label: BTO flat waiting times
sections.summary: Most BTO flat buyers can move in within four to five years after booking, and up to 23,000 new BTO flats will be launched yearly in 2022 and 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For ongoing BTO projects, most flat buyers will be able to move into their new homes within four to five years after booking their flats, barring further unforeseen circumstances.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will also launch up to 23,000 new BTO flats per year in 2022 and 2023 as MND has indicated.

sections.label: Fathers' paternity leave utilisation
sections.summary: Research shows workplace support is a key factor affecting fathers' utilisation of paternity leave across jobs and companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Our research on the experiences of fathers' use of paternity leave shows that, across different types of jobs and companies, a key factor affecting the level of utilisation is workplace support.

sections.label: Flexible paternity and childcare leave
sections.summary: Employers could let fathers take paternity leave in more than one period within the child's first year, and the Government will review parental leave and encourage employer flexibility instead of legislating more childcare leave.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In such situations, employers could exercise more flexibility in fathers' utilisation of paternity leave, such as taking the leave in more than one period within their child's first year, to minimise disruptions to business operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will consider Mr Louis Ng's feedback, continue to review the scope for more parental leave provisions and work with employers to encourage their utilisation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Instead of legislating more childcare leave, the Government aims to lead by example and encourage employers to follow suit by exercising more flexibility and extending childcare leave where possible.

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements norm
sections.summary: The pandemic has created a window of opportunity to make flexible work arrangements a norm, with more to be shared in the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: With new work practices thrust upon us by the pandemic, we now have a window of opportunity to make FWAs a norm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will be working with employers to do so, and more will be shared in the White Paper on Singapore Women's Development which will be tabled in Parliament later this year.

sections.label: Citizenships granted in 2021
sections.summary: About 21,500 new citizenships were granted in 2021, slightly lower than pre-COVID-19 levels, and immigration policy will remain measured and stable.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In 2021, we granted about 21,500 new citizenships, including about 1,200 citizenships to children born overseas to Singaporean parents.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: During last year’s Committee of Supply (COS), I said that a few thousand applicants who were approved in-principle in 2020 had not completed all the required processes to be granted PR or citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: These applicants were, subsequently, granted PR or citizenship, adding to the numbers granted in 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: Nonetheless, the total number of Singapore Citizenships (SCs) granted in 2021 remains slightly lower than pre-COVID-19 levels, as those granted SCs must first renounce their foreign citizenship.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: In some cases, this continues to take longer than usual due to COVID-19 related measures.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: We will continue to ensure that our immigration policy remains relevant to our needs and keeps the pace of immigration measured and stable.

sections.label: MOM OneWorkplace.sg initiative
sections.summary: MOM's OneWorkplace.sg gives employers tools and resources to find workplace integration gaps and run team-bonding and CSR activities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister, Prime Minister's Office (Ms Indranee Rajah)
sentences.text: For example, MOM’s OneWorkplace.sg initiative provides employers with tools and resources to identify workplace integration gaps and implement team-bonding programmes and Corporate Social Responsibility activities.

sections.label: PA budget and other ministries
sections.summary: The People's Association has a $908 million budget, while MCCY and MSF separately serve community engagement and citizens' welfare with $107 million and $611 million.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The People's Association (PA), with its $908 million budget, comes to mind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Community engagement and citizens' welfare are very important, but they are separately served by MCCY and MSF, with budgets of $107 million and $611 million respectively.

sections.label: FY2022 development budget
sections.summary: For FY2022, another $197 million is budgeted for such development.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: For FY2022, another $197 million is budgeted for such development.

sections.label: Moving SkillsFuture and ECDA budgets
sections.summary: The $679 million for SkillsFuture should move from MOE to MOM, and the $1.6 billion for ECDA from MSF to MOE.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The $679 million earmarked for SkillsFuture should be taken out of MOE and integrated into MOM to ensure that the spending creates jobs for Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Leong Mun Wai (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The $1.6 billion earmarked for Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) can be taken out of MSF and integrated into MOE, to create a seamless education and development curriculum for our children.

sections.label: Work from Anywhere and PSD
sections.summary: The speaker highlighted COVID-19 accelerating the Work from Anywhere trend and asked PSD's plans to prepare public officers for tomorrow's challenges.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, in my Budget debate speech, I highlighted how COVID-19 has accelerated the Work from Anywhere trend and how this has spawned a trending culture of "workcations" and countries chasing to attract digital nomads.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: What are PSD’s plans to ensure that our public officers of today will be ready to take on the challenges of tomorrow?

sections.label: Hiring overseas digital nomads
sections.summary: The question asks whether the Public Service will hire Singaporean digital nomads based overseas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Will the Public Service hire Singaporean digital nomads based overseas?

sections.label: Public Service attrition and burnout
sections.summary: The resignation rate in the Management Executive scheme reached a 10-year high of 9.9% in 2021, and PSD is asked what it is doing about burnout.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Lastly, I note with concern that our Public Service is experiencing an unusual rise in attrition, with the resignation rate in the Management Executive scheme reaching a 10-year high of 9.9% in 2021.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: If so, what is PSD doing to alleviate burnout in the service?

sections.label: Cross-deployment of public officers
sections.summary: A few thousand public officers have been cross-deployed beyond their normal duties to manage the crisis and continue doing so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: In fact, a few thousand officers from the Public Service have been cross-deployed to different positions beyond their previous normal duties in order to help out and manage the crisis and they continue to do this even as we speak.

sections.label: Expansion to 16 Government initiatives
sections.summary: The effort has expanded to cover 16 Government initiatives today, including the CDC Vouchers Merchants GoWhere.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Since then, we have expanded to cover 16 Government initiatives today, including the recent CDC Vouchers Merchants GoWhere.

sections.label: Our Tampines Hub centre services
sections.summary: Since 2018, the Centre at Our Tampines Hub has expanded to provide 400 services across 19 agencies for citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Since 2018, the Centre at Our Tampines Hub has expanded to provide 400 services across 19 agencies for our citizens.

sections.label: GoBusiness e-services access
sections.summary: Developed by MTI and SNDGG, GoBusiness lets users access information on over 300 Government-to-Business e-services.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Developed by MTI and the Smart Nation and Digital Government Group (SNDGG), GoBusiness allows users to access information of over 300 Government-to-Business e-services.

sections.label: 40 hours for developmental activities
sections.summary: Starting this year, each public officer may use up to 40 hours a year for developmental activities with private, social and non-profit organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And this is how we are also executing our plans to manage COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Therefore, starting from this year, we will allow each public officer to use up to 40 hours a year to participate in developmental activities with the private, social and non-profit organisations.

sections.label: Public officers developmental activities
sections.summary: From this year, every public officer can use up to 40 hours a year for developmental activities with private, social and non-profit organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: And that is why, to this end, I want to further this connection between the Public Service and the sector and organisations beyond the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: That is why, from this year onwards, every public officer will be able to use up to 40 hours a year to participate in developmental activities with the private, social and non-profit organisations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: These opportunities can be made available by the Public Service Division and other agencies, or self-sourced opportunities, as long as the activities are developmental and do not lead to any conflict of interests.

sections.label: PA staff and volunteers
sections.summary: There are only about 2,000 PA staff, but many volunteers were mobilised to come together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We did not depend just on the PA staff.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: There are only about 2,000 PA staff but there are many volunteers that we mobilised to come together.

sections.label: Guarding against complacency
sections.summary: The Public Service will keep checking blind spots and taking ideas from within and beyond the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We are constantly guarding against complacency and we constantly want to do better for Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will constantly check our blind spots, take in the best ideas from within this Chamber, from the Public Service itself and from people and organisations beyond the Public Service.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: Because our goal is to make sure that we have a Public Service that Singaporeans can be proud of and that can do justice to the potential of Singapore and Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Chan Chun Sing)
sentences.text: We will continue to work on that basis to adjust and adapt flexibly according to the circumstances.

sections.label: Smart Nation review
sections.summary: Smart Nation is in its fifth year and is undergoing a review, with results to be updated later.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, Smart Nation is in its fifth year and it is undergoing a review so that we can also chart the next bound.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: This review, the results of it, we will be able to update Members at a later date and I would leave it till then.

sections.label: E-residency benefits unclear
sections.summary: It is not clear what the benefits and obligations are for e-residents.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Nevertheless, let me share some of my own observations about e-residency.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I think it is not clear what the benefits and obligations are for the e-residents.

sections.label: E-residency design clarity
sections.summary: There is no clarity about what the e-residency design should involve and what benefits and obligations it should confer.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Then, having allowed these e-residents to earn income from Singapore and yet the e-residents will not have the opportunity to consume in Singapore, the benefits become much more questionable.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I will just say, at this point in time, that there is no clarity about what this design of the e-residency should involve and what benefits and obligations it should confer.
